title: sinpi
summary: Compute sin(X*pi) accurately with exact integer and half-integer results.

gpu_support.notes: gpuArray inputs are gathered to the host so RunMat can preserve exact results at integer and half-integer multiples of pi.

fusion.notes: Fusion is intentionally disabled because lowering to `sin(X*pi)` would lose the exactness guarantees that distinguish `sinpi` from `sin`.

description: `sinpi(X)` computes `sin(X*pi)` without first materializing the approximate floating-point value `X*pi`. Integers return exactly zero and odd half-integers return exactly `+1` or `-1`.
behaviors: Operates element-wise on scalars, vectors, matrices, and N-D tensors.

The documented R2026a input classes are single and double. Integer, logical, and character inputs are RunMat extensions; integer arrays return exact double zeros directly from native storage, including values above the exact binary64 range.
Returns exactly 0 for integer inputs and exactly ±1 for odd half-integer inputs.
Complex inputs use the analytic extension of `sin(pi*z)` while preserving exact real-axis sine/cosine factors when possible.
Output shape matches the input shape; non-finite real inputs produce `NaN`.
String inputs are unsupported and raise a builtin-scoped error.

examples.description: Avoid floating-point drift at integer multiples

faqs.question: Why use `sinpi(X)` instead of `sin(X*pi)`?
faqs.answer: `pi` is not exactly representable in binary floating point. `sinpi` short-circuits integer and half-integer multiples so common exact results do not contain small rounding noise.

faqs.question: Does `sinpi` support gpuArray inputs?
faqs.answer: Yes. RunMat currently gathers gpuArray inputs and evaluates the exact host implementation; no GPU kernel is launched yet.
